content:
maria: kicking off a compact field brief for enterprise buyers — goal: single-sheet sales brief + short benchmark narrative + webinar seed copy + inbound routing map. target customers: security-sensitive fintech / health platforms. keep it <1 page.
elaine: love it. can we include a tiny SLA matrix and deployment decision flow (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? sales asks for a one-line migration path.
sam: i can draft the benchmark bullet points — will include 99p latency, median cost/token vs typical self-hosted, and a short robustness/rollback line. need the workload to benchmark (chat + retrieval + embeddings).
raj: add a short note on control-plane options and KMS/HSM integrations. also add the canary/fallback routing highlight — customers care about graceful degradation.
maria: outline i propose (super compact):
  - top blurb: problem + our positioning (one sentence)
  - 3 proof bullets (latency, cost, uptime)
  - deployment snapshot (hosted / dedicated / private) with one-line tradeoffs
  - security callouts (data at rest, KMS, SOC/ISO statements)
  - SLA table (p50/p95/p99 targets + credits line)
  - recommended next step (webinar signup / field demo contact)
elaine: that works. for routing: we need lead tags so AE queues route correctly. mapping: 
  sales_region -> us/eu/apac
  deploy_intent -> hosted/dedicated/private
  compliance -> pci/hipaa/sox
  target_vertical -> fintech/health/saas

sam: benchmark bullets draft: 
  - "99th percentile tail: <120ms token latency on LlamaX-13B quantized, standard chat workload"
  - "Cost/unit: ~0.6x of typical self-hosted with moderate batching and prefix cache"
  - "Regression guard: integrated evals + canary model rollouts reduced quality regressions by 18% in internal tests"

maria: nice. keep the numbers conservative and cite internal test note. add a tiny footnote: "internal lab workload: 8k daily active chat sessions, 30-token median responses"
raj: for deployment snapshot, short lines: 
  - Hosted API — fastest time to value, pay-as-you-go, shared infra, quick benchmarks
  - Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency targets
  - Private — customer-managed VPC or on-prem; full control over networking + KMS; recommended for regulated workloads
elaine: SLA table suggestion (super condensed):
  - Availability: Hosted 99.9%, Dedicated 99.95%, Private (depends on infra)
  - Latency SLO: p95 hosted ~150ms, dedicated p95 ~100ms, private depends on customer infra
  - Credits: standard 10% for major violations (TBD legal)

maria: webinar seed copy (short):
  - headline: "Serving LLMs in Regulated Environments: Balancing Latency, Cost, and Control"
  - 2-sentence description: "Join Redwood product and infra leads for a practical playbook to deploy LLMs behind strict security and SLA requirements. We’ll show benchmarks, tradeoffs across deployment modes, and real routing patterns for high-availability apps."
  - CTA: "Register — limited seats" with form capturing mapping fields above

elaine: inbound form fields for marketing automation (minimal): name, email, company, role, region, deploy_intent, compliance_needs, expected_qps, budget_range. funnel tags -> salesforce lead owner by region + deploy_intent. can opsbot drop an example mapping?
opsbot: mapping snippet: 
```yaml
lead_routing:
  - condition: region == "EU"
    owner: "EMEA_AE_Pool"
  - condition: deploy_intent == "private" and compliance_needs == "hipaa"
    owner: "Healthcare_Expert_AE"
  - else:
    owner: "Global_PLG_AE"
```

sam: for the benchmark narrative block (1 short paragraph):
  "In internal tests simulating 8k daily active chat sessions and a mixed retrieval workload, Redwood delivered consistent p95 latency reductions vs baseline self-hosted setups while lowering per-token cost through continuous batching and prefix caching. The combination of model-variant routing and canary rollouts enabled safe updates with measurable reductions in quality regressions."

maria: perfect. can we also add a 1-line objection handling bank? (security, cost, vendor lock-in)
raj: quick lines: 
  - security: "Private deploy + KMS + audit logs; SOC/ISO compliance support and data residency options."
  - cost: "SLA-backed dedicated tiers + Optimize suggestions (quantize/batching) to reduce unit economics."
  - lock-in: "Open model catalog + exportable model artifacts; routing policies let you fallback to cheaper variants."

elaine: logistics: we want this out to field next tuesday. final brief + design handed off friday COB. who owns final copy and SF mapping?
maria: i’ll own final copy and webinar copy. elaine you own routing + SF mapping. sam finalize benchmark bullets and the single-paragraph narrative. raj review security lines.
elaine: ack. i’ll post the mapping file in the /marketing/ops folder and tag ops and sales.
sam: will drop benchmark bullets by tomorrow EOD.
raj: will review security language by friday morning.
maria: thanks team — small format brief, big impact. tagging salesops for visibility: @elaine FYI. planning small playbook PDF + 1-slide cheat sheet for demos.
elaine: :thumbsup:
opsbot: reminder: marketing campaign "field-quickbrief-mar-214876" scheduled to start 2148800000 (automated).
